'''Jonathan Balcombe''' (born 28 February 1959) is an [[Ethology|ethologist]] and author. He is formerly director of animal sentience with the Humane Society Institute for Science and Policy, and department chair for animal studies with Humane Society University,<ref>[http://www.humanesocietyuniversity.org/academics/sce/webinars/business_of_humane_education_webinar.aspx Humane Society University]</ref> in [[Washington, DC]].<ref name="Washington Post" />  He lectures internationally on animal behavior and the [[human-animal relationship]]. He also served as associate editor of the journal ''Animal Sentience'' from 2015 to 2019.

==Biography==

Balcombe was born in [[Hornchurch|Hornchurch, England]].<ref name="The Guardian">{{cite news|last=Randerson|first=James|title=Jonathan Balcombe: 'Stop being beastly to hens'|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2010/apr/25/jonathan-balcombe-animal-feelings|work=The Guardian|access-date=11 July 2013|location=London|date=25 April 2010}}</ref>  He grew up in New Zealand and Canada before settling in the United States in 1987.<ref name="The Press Enterprise" />

Balcombe earned a Bachelor of Science degree in [[biology]] in 1983 from [[Faculty of Environmental Studies|York University]] in Toronto, then a Master of Science in biology from [[Carleton University]] in Ottawa in 1987. In 1991, he completed a Ph.D in [[ethology]] (animal behavior) at the [[East Tennessee University|University of Tennessee]],<ref name="Washington Post">{{cite news|last=Duin|first=Julia|title=Humane Society University in D.C. is a pioneer in the growing animal studies movement|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/magazine/humane-society-university-in-dc-is-a-pioneer-in-the-growing-animal-studies-movement/2012/04/10/gIQAnnUwET_story.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130214061015/http://articles.washingtonpost.com/2012-04-13/lifestyle/35452419_1_animal-rescue-animal-behavior-animal-abuse|url-status=live|archive-date=14 February 2013|newspaper=The Washington Post|access-date=12 July 2013|date=14 April 2012}}</ref>  where he studied mother-pup vocal communication in the [[Mexican Free-tailed Bat|Mexican free-tailed bat]].<ref name="The Press Enterprise">{{cite web|title=REDLANDS: University hosts 'Animals, Society' lecture series|url=http://www.pe.com/local-news/local-news-headlines/20120919-redlands-university-hosts-animals-society-lecture-series.ece|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140906112203/http://www.pe.com/articles/animals-650903-animal-university.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 September 2014|publisher=The Press Enterprise|access-date=12 July 2013}}</ref><ref name=NBC>{{cite web|last=Viegas|first=Jennifer|title=Bats like to hang out with their friends, too|date=9 February 2011 |url=http://www.nbcnews.com/id/41492997/ns/technology_and_science-science/t/bats-hang-out-their-friends-too/#.UeBDbXr7RBw|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140906085406/http://www.nbcnews.com/id/41492997/ns/technology_and_science-science/t/bats-hang-out-their-friends-too/#.UeBDbXr7RBw|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 September 2014|publisher=NBC|access-date=12 July 2013}}</ref>

Balcombe has worked for several animal protection organizations, including [[The Humane Society of the United States]], [[Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine]], and [[People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals]]. He also worked as a research coordinator and grant writer for Immersion Medical, a for-profit company that makes virtual reality training simulators for minimally-invasive surgery.<ref name=Immersion>{{cite web|last=Balcombe|first=Jonathan|title=Dissection: The Scientific Case|url=http://www.animalsandsociety.org/files/Balcombe,%20Jonathan,%20Dissection%20The%20Scientific%20Case%20for%20Alternatives,%20JAAWS%204-2,%202001.pdf|work=Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science|publisher=Routledge|access-date=16 May 2014}}</ref> In addition to writing books, Jonathan currently does professional editing for aspiring and established authors. He also teaches a course in animal sentience for the Viridis Graduate Institute.

Balcombe has been a [[Veganism|vegan]] since 1989.<ref>[https://www.veggievision.tv/exclusive-interview-with-the-amazing-jonathan-balcombe-author-of-what-a-fish-knows/ "Exclusive Interview with the Amazing Jonathan Balcombe – Author of What A Fish Knows"]. veggievision.tv. Retrieved 26 October 2022.</ref>

==Writing==

Balcombe's first book, ''The Use of Animals in Higher Education: Problems, Alternatives, and Recommendations'', was published by Humane Society Press in 2000. His trade book, ''Pleasurable Kingdom: Animals and the Nature of Feeling Good'', was released by [[Macmillan Publishers|Macmillan]] in 2006. The book details Balcombe's positions on the [[sentience]] of animals, and the existence of pleasure seeking behavior, in contrast with the behavioralist mainstream, which rejects [[anthropomorphism]] of animals.<ref name="Sydney Morning Herald">{{cite news|last=Robinson|first=Nicola|title=Pleasurable Kingdom|url=http://www.smh.com.au/news/book-reviews/pleasurable-kingdom/2007/08/06/1186252588627.html|publisher=Sydney Morning Herald|access-date=11 July 2013|date=6 August 2007}}</ref>  Deutschlandradio called the book a "convincing and a fun read."<ref name=Deutschlandradio>{{cite web|last=Lange|first=Michael|title=Vergnügen als Evolutionsvorteil|url=http://www.dradio.de/dkultur/sendungen/kritik/722719/|work=Radiofeuilleton: Kritik|publisher=Deutschlandradio|access-date=11 July 2013}}</ref>

In 2010, Balcombe published ''Second Nature: The Inner Lives of Animals'', in which he surveys recent scientific discoveries about animal [[cognition]], [[emotion]], and [[virtue]], and aims to "protest against what he sees as an unbroken tradition of human cruelty and indifference."<ref name=Scotman>{{cite web|title=Book review: Second Nature: The Inner Lives of Animals|url=http://www.scotsman.com/lifestyle/books/features/book-review-second-nature-the-inner-lives-of-animals-1-474944|work=lifestyle.scotsman.com|publisher=Scotsman|access-date=11 July 2013}}</ref>

''[[The Exultant Ark]]: A Pictorial Tour of Animal Pleasure'' was released in 2011 by the University of California Press. Using images of contented animals in their natural environment, Balcombe "proves that animals aren’t always engaged in a battle for survival but will frequently do things for nothing more than the feeling of satisfaction."<ref name="The Ecologist">{{cite web|last=Phillips|first=Robert|title=The Exultant Ark: A Pictorial Tour of Animal Pleasure|date=28 October 2011 |url=http://www.theecologist.org/reviews/books/1110526/the_exultant_ark_a_pictorial_tour_of_animal_pleasure.html|publisher=The Ecologist|access-date=12 July 2013}}</ref> Balcombe disputes the mainstream scientific community's belief that the animal kingdom is an unforgiving struggle for survival. The book briefly broke into the top 100 on Amazon.com following favorable reviews in ''[[The New York Times]]'' and the ''[[New York Post]].''<ref name="The New York Post">{{cite news|last=Callahan|first=Maureen|title=Birds do it, Bees do it|url=http://www.nypost.com/p/news/opinion/opedcolumnists/birds_do_it_bees_do_it_gmtX6T7bitrT3LBNcCJTkN|publisher=The New York Post|access-date=12 July 2013}}</ref><ref name="The New York Times">{{cite news|last=Bouton|first=Katherine|title=The Joy of a Sun Bath, a Snuggle, a Bite of Pâté|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/07/19/science/19scibooks.html?_r=0|work=The New York Times|access-date=12 July 2013|date=18 July 2011}}</ref>

Balcombe's 2016 book, ''What A Fish Knows'', combines science and story-telling to examine the inner lives of the world's most diverse group of vertebrates.<ref>{{cite news |last=Balcombe |first=Jonathan |date=15 May 2016 |title=Fishes Have Feelings, Too |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/05/15/opinion/fishes-have-feelings-too.html |newspaper=NYT |access-date=15 May 2016 }}</ref>  ''What A Fish Knows'' has a release date of 7 June 2016, from Scientific American/Farrar, Straus and Giroux.

Balcombe has published over 60 scholarly articles and book chapters on various topics, including animal behavior, animal research, [[Vivisection|animal dissection]], medical simulation, and [[veganism]].<ref name="The Press Enterprise" /> His essay titled "After Meat" appears in the 2016 book "Impact of Meat Consumption on Health and Environmental Sustainability," edited by Dora Marinova and Talia Raphaely.

== Advocacy ==

Balcombe uses a variety of platforms to advocate for a sea-change in the human-animal relationship. In addition to his books and journal papers, he is a regular speaker at conferences, campuses, public schools and other venues. He is interviewed often in the media, and he has written blogs for ''[[Psychology Today]]'', One Green Planet, Secretary of Innovation, and [[Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine]]. He is a manuscript reviewer for scholarly journals such as [[Animal Behaviour (journal)|''Animal Behaviour'']], the ''Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science'', and the ''[[Journal of Consciousness Studies]]''.
